knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Until the current formal instruction is obtained from the clinical lead or IPC contact, the restricted area does not start. A heard rumour and an unchanged schedule do not govern, so the cleaner gets the instruction first.
The outbreak instruction names the product for the handrail. The cleaner does not substitute, tells the supervisor so the named product is supplied, and postpones the handrail.
The current formal instruction from the facility's clinical or IPC lead governs cleaning during an outbreak. A verbal message and a schedule prepared before the outbreak do not govern.

practicalCriteria: Given a rumour of an outbreak with an unchanged schedule that lists a resident room, the learner does not start the room until it has the current formal instruction from the clinical lead or IPC contact.
Given an outbreak instruction that names a product not on the trolley, the learner does not substitute, and tells the supervisor so the named product is supplied.
The learner does not carry dedicated equipment from a restricted area into a clean area.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80% pass mark, which for three checks means all three correct. Practical competence needs facility-observed assessment against the practical criteria, and a knowledge pass does not count as practical competence.
evidenceRequired: Record showing the instruction source and time before the restricted area was started
Record of the postponed handrail with the shortfall and time
Observation note of the dedicated-equipment handling
stopWorkCriteria: Learner starts a restricted area on a rumour or an unchanged schedule
Learner uses a product that the outbreak instruction does not name
Learner carries dedicated equipment from a restricted area into a clean area
